item.title: agentmemory: Persistent Memory for AI Coding Agents
item.description:
agentmemory is an open-source memory server that gives AI coding agents persistent memory across sessions. Hooks in Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Hermes, OpenClaw and other agents record what the agent does, and the server injects the most relevant past context when the next session starts. You install it with npx -y @agentmemory/agentmemory@latest.

The project lives at github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory, is written in TypeScript under the Apache 2.0 license, and had about 29,300 GitHub stars on 12 October 2026. This page covers what it does, how it works, how to set it up, what its benchmark numbers mean, and how it compares with Hindsight and Mem0 for coding-agent memory. Facts come from the agentmemory README and benchmark files, checked on 12 October 2026. (This site, aiagentmemory.org, has no connection to the agentmemory project.)

item.title: Claude Code Memory: CLAUDE.md, Auto Memory and Plugins
item.description:
Claude Code memory is two built-in systems. CLAUDE.md files hold instructions you write, and Claude Code loads them at the start of every session. Auto memory holds notes Claude writes for itself in ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/. You manage both with /memory. For more than notes, add a memory MCP server or a plugin such as claude-mem or Hindsight.

Each Claude Code session starts with an empty context window, so anything Claude should know has to come from a file that loads back in. This page covers how Claude Code’s built-in memory works, from Anthropic’s Claude Code memory docs, then the add-on options and how they compare. All facts were checked on 12 October 2026. For how other coding agents (Cursor, Copilot) handle memory, see AI coding agent memory. The Claude chat app at claude.ai has its own, separate memory feature, covered in Claude AI long-term memory.

item.title: AI Memory MCP Servers: Official Server and Alternatives
item.description:
An AI memory MCP server is a Model Context Protocol server that gives any MCP client tools to save and recall memories. Instead of each app building its own memory, Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor or a custom agent connect to the same server and call tools like add_observations or search_nodes. The official reference server stores a small knowledge graph in a JSONL file.

This page explains how memory over MCP works, walks through the official server, compares the main alternatives, and covers security. Facts come from each project’s README, checked October 2026.
